title: Realizing Joint Extreme-Scale Simulations on Multiple Supercomputers - Two Superfacility Case Studies
problem: High-dimensional grid-based simulations suffer from the curse of dimensionality and require intractable computational resources with full-grid solvers (>1,000 nonillion DOF per system). Coordinating simulations across multiple heterogeneous supercomputers introduces challenges in load balancing, communication bandwidth, memory utilization, and I/O management.
motivation: Combining multiple supercomputers into superfacility environments enables high-fidelity, extreme-scale simulations across scientific domains that would otherwise be computationally intractable.
method: The combination technique partitions an extremely large high-dimensional grid across multiple supercomputers, with each computing a complete subgrid at full resolution. To coordinate work across these diverse machines, it uses load balancing to keep all systems equally busy, compresses data flowing between supercomputers to maximize network throughput, intelligently routes I/O operations to match each machine's strengths, and optimizes the algorithm itself for memory efficiency. The technique extends to work with three or more supercomputers simultaneously.
key_novelty: The key innovation is extending the combination technique to coordinate three or more supercomputers for extreme-scale high-dimensional simulations in a superfacility (a coordinated network of supercomputers).
contributions: Extended combination technique enabling 3+ supercomputers to jointly solve high-dimensional simulations
Load balancing and compression strategies for heterogeneous superfacility environments
Hardware-aware I/O management and memory optimization techniques
Demonstrated extreme-scale feasibility: 46 trillion DOF on two systems, 35 trillion DOF on three systems

metrics.other: extreme-scale simulations: 46 trillion DOF (2 systems), 35 trillion DOF (3 systems)

primary_theme: distributed extreme-scale HPC via multi-system combination technique
